questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The periodic time of a magnet in vibration magnetometer is $T_0$. If a magnet is replaced by another magnet whose moment of inertia is three times and magnetic moment is one-third of the original magnet, then time period of new magnet will be
questions.solution:
The time period of a magnet in a vibration magnetometer is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MB_H}}$

For the original magnet, $T_0 = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MB_H}}$

For the new magnet, the moment of inertia is $I' = 3I$ and the magnetic moment is $M' = \dfrac{M}{3}$

The new time period is $T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{I'}{M'B_H}}$

Substituting the values, $T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{3I}{\left(\dfrac{M}{3}\right)B_H}}$

$T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{9I}{MB_H}}$

$T' = 3 \times 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MB_H}}$

$T' = 3T_0$

Answer: $3\,T_0$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The frequency of oscillation of a small magnet in a magnetic field of induction 'B' is '$n$'. If the frequency of oscillations of the same magnet in a field of induction 'X' falls to $\left(\dfrac{n}{3}\right)$, the value of 'X' is
questions.solution:
The frequency of oscillation of a magnet in a magnetic field is given by

$n = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{MB}{I}}$

Since the same magnet is used, $M$ and $I$ are constant. Thus, $n \propto \sqrt{B}$, which implies $B \propto n^2$.

Given $n_1 = n$ at $B_1 = B$, and $n_2 = \dfrac{n}{3}$ at $B_2 = X$.

$\dfrac{B_1}{B_2} = \left(\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}\right)^2$

$\dfrac{B}{X} = \left(\dfrac{n}{n/3}\right)^2 = 3^2 = 9$

$X = \dfrac{B}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{B}{9}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A diamagnetic liquid is filled in a U-tube. One arm of a U-tube is placed in an external magnetic field with the meniscus in line with the field. The level of the liquid in that arm will
questions.solution:
Diamagnetic substances are repelled by magnetic fields and tend to move from regions of stronger magnetic field to regions of weaker magnetic field.

When one arm of the U-tube containing a diamagnetic liquid is placed in an external magnetic field, the liquid experiences a force pushing it away from the stronger field region.

As a result, the level of the liquid in the arm placed in the magnetic field will fall.

Answer: fall.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The region inside a current carrying toroid is filled with a material (Niobium) having susceptibility $\chi = 2.6 \times 10^{-5}$. The percentage increase in the magnetic field in the presence of Niobium over that without it, is
questions.solution:
The magnetic field inside a toroid without any material is given by $B_0 = \mu_0 n I$.

When the toroid is filled with a material of magnetic susceptibility $\chi$, the magnetic field becomes $B = \mu_0 (1 + \chi) n I$.

The increase in the magnetic field is $\Delta B = B - B_0 = \mu_0 \chi n I = B_0 \chi$.

The percentage increase in the magnetic field is $\dfrac{\Delta B}{B_0} \times 100 = \chi \times 100$.

Substituting the given value of susceptibility $\chi = 2.6 \times 10^{-5}$:

Percentage increase $= 2.6 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 2.6 \times 10^{-3}$.

Answer: $2.6 \times 10^{-3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An iron rod is placed parallel to magnetic field intensity 1000 A/m. The magnetic flux through the rod is $3 \times 10^{-4}$ Wb and its cross-sectional area is $1.5\ \text{cm}^2$. The magnetic permeability of rod in $\text{Wb/}_{\text{A-m}}$ is
questions.solution:
Given magnetic field intensity $H = 1000$ A/m.

Magnetic flux $\Phi = 3 \times 10^{-4}$ Wb.

Cross-sectional area $A = 1.5 \text{ cm}^2 = 1.5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$.

The magnetic induction $B$ is given by $B = \dfrac{\Phi}{A}$.

Substituting the values:

$B = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{-4}}{1.5 \times 10^{-4}} = 2$ Wb/m$^2$.

The magnetic permeability $\mu$ is given by $\mu = \dfrac{B}{H}$.

$\mu = \dfrac{2}{1000} = 2 \times 10^{-3}$ Wb/(A-m).

Answer: $2 \times 10^{-3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The product of magnetic susceptibility (\chi$) and absolute temperature (T) is constant for a$
options: paramagnetic as well as ferromagnetic substance.
questions.solution:
According to Curie's law, the magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) of a paramagnetic substance is inversely proportional to its absolute temperature ($T$).

$\chi \propto \dfrac{1}{T}$

$\chi = \dfrac{C}{T}$

$\chi T = C$

where $C$ is Curie's constant. Thus, the product of magnetic susceptibility and absolute temperature is constant for a paramagnetic substance.

For diamagnetic substances, susceptibility is independent of temperature. For ferromagnetic substances, susceptibility follows the Curie-Weiss law ($\chi = \dfrac{C}{T - T_c}$) above the Curie temperature.

Answer: paramagnetic substance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An iron rod is placed parallel to magnetic field intensity 2000 A/m. The magnetic flux through rod is $6 \times 10^{-4}$ wb and its cross sectional area is 3 cm^2. The magnetic permeability of the rod in wb/A-m is
questions.solution:
Given magnetic field intensity $H = 2000$ A/m

Magnetic flux $\Phi = 6 \times 10^{-4}$ Wb

Cross-sectional area $A = 3$ cm$^2 = 3 \times 10^{-4}$ m$^2$

Magnetic induction $B$ is given by $B = \dfrac{\Phi}{A}$

$B = \dfrac{6 \times 10^{-4}}{3 \times 10^{-4}} = 2$ Wb/m$^2$

Magnetic permeability $\mu$ is given by $\mu = \dfrac{B}{H}$

$\mu = \dfrac{2}{2000} = 10^{-3}$ Wb/A-m

Answer: $10^{-3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic field (B) inside a long solenoid having ' n ' turns per unit length and carrying current ' $i$ ' when iron core is kept in it, is (\mu_0=$ permeability of vacuum, \chi=$ magnetic susceptibility)
questions.solution:
Magnetic field enhancement in a solenoid with an iron core

The magnetic field inside a long solenoid with n turns per unit length carrying current i is given by $B_0 = \mu_0 n i$.

Introducing an iron core changes the permeability from $\mu_0$ to $\mu$, so the field becomes $B = \mu n i$.

The permeability of a magnetic material is defined by $\mu = \mu_0 (1 + \chi)$, where $\chi$ is the magnetic susceptibility.

Substituting this into the equation for the magnetic field yields $B = \mu_0 (1 + \chi) n i$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: ' $\chi_1{ }^{\prime},{ }^{\prime} \chi_2{ }^{\prime}$ and ' $\chi_3{ }^{\prime}$ are susceptibilities of a paramagnetic material at temperatures ' $\mathrm{T}_1{ }^{\prime} \mathrm{K}$, ' $\mathrm{T}_2{ }^{\prime} \mathrm{K}$ and ' $\mathrm{T}_3{ }^{\prime} \mathrm{K}$ respectively, then
questions.solution:
For a paramagnetic material, the magnetic susceptibility $\chi = \frac{C}{T}$ follows Curie's Law, where $C$ is the Curie constant.

The ratio $\frac{\chi_1}{\chi_2} = \frac{C / T_1}{C / T_2} = \frac{T_2}{T_1}$, so $\chi_1 : \chi_2 = T_2 : T_1$.

Similarly, $\frac{\chi_2}{\chi_3} = \frac{T_3}{T_2}$, giving $\chi_2 : \chi_3 = T_3 : T_2$.

These relationships correspond to option C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bar of iron having magnetic moment $2 \cdot 4 \mathrm{Am}^2$ weighs 66 g. If the density of the material of the bar is $7700 \mathrm{ kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$, the intensity of magnetisation in $\mathrm{Am}^{-1}$ is
questions.solution:
The intensity of magnetization $I$ is defined as the magnetic moment per unit volume, given by $I = M/V$.

Given the magnetic moment $M = 2.4\,\mathrm{Am}^2$, mass $m = 66\,\mathrm{g} = 66 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{kg}$, and density $\rho = 7700\,\mathrm{kg/m}^3$, the volume is calculated as $V = m/\rho$.

$V = \frac{66 \times 10^{-3}}{7700} = \frac{66}{7700} \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m}^3 = \frac{6}{7} \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m}^3$

Substituting into the magnetization formula yields:

$I = \frac{2.4}{\frac{6}{7} \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{2.4 \times 7}{6} \times 10^5 = 2.8 \times 10^5\,\mathrm{Am}^{-1}$

This result corresponds to option B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: To protect the instrument from magnetic field, it is completely surrounded by
questions.solution:
Magnetic shielding requires surrounding the instrument with a high permeability material that diverts external field lines. Soft ferromagnetic materials exhibit this property due to their exceptionally high magnetic permeability.

When placed in an external magnetic field, soft ferromagnetic substances channel field lines through themselves, reducing the field strength within the enclosed region to negligible levels.

Diamagnetic and paramagnetic materials possess much lower permeabilities and are ineffective for this purpose. The appropriate choice is therefore a soft ferromagnetic substance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Magnetic hysteresis is exhibited by magnetic materials which are
questions.solution:
Magnetic hysteresis occurs when a material's magnetization depends on its magnetic history, not just the current applied field, resulting in a characteristic lag that forms a hysteresis loop when plotted.

This phenomenon is exclusive to ferromagnetic materials, which contain permanent magnetic dipoles organized into domains. Under an external magnetic field, these domains align and grow, producing strong magnetization. When the field is removed, residual magnetization (retentivity) persists due to sustained domain alignment, requiring an opposite coercive field to neutralize it.

In contrast, paramagnetic and diamagnetic materials lack this memory effect; their magnetization is proportional to the applied field and vanishes upon its removal.

$\therefore$ The correct option is C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Susceptibility of a paramagnetic substance is
questions.solution:
The magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ is defined as $\chi = M/H$, where $M$ is magnetization and $H$ is magnetic field strength.

Paramagnetic materials exhibit atomic magnetic dipoles that align with an applied magnetic field, resulting in magnetization $M$ parallel to $H$. Since both quantities share the same direction, $\chi > 0$.

This alignment is partial and produces weak magnetization, making $\chi$ small in magnitude.

Option analysis:

A) Negative and large – incorrect, characteristic of diamagnetism
B) Negative and small – incorrect, diamagnetic property
C) Positive and large – incorrect, describes ferromagnetism
D) Positive and small – correct

The susceptibility of a paramagnetic substance is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

questions.q: The space within the current carrying toroid is filled with aluminium of susceptibility ' $\chi$ '. The percentage increase in the magnetic field ' $B$ ' will be
questions.solution:
The magnetic field inside a toroidal coil in vacuum is given by $B_0 = \mu_0 n I$, with $n$ representing the number of turns per unit length and $I$ the current.

When the interior is filled with a material of magnetic permeability $\mu$, the field becomes $B = \mu n I$.
Using the relation $\mu = \mu_0 (1 + \chi)$, where $\chi$ is the magnetic susceptibility, this gives $B = \mu_0 (1 + \chi) n I$.

Expressing this in terms of $B_0$ yields $B = (1 + \chi) B_0$.
The increase in magnetic field is therefore $\Delta B = B - B_0 = \chi B_0$.

The percentage increase is:
$\frac{\Delta B}{B_0} \times 100\% = \chi \times 100\%$.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The variation of magnetic susceptibility $(\chi)$ with temperature for a diamagnetic substance is shown correctly by graph
questions.solution:
The magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ of a diamagnetic substance is a small, negative quantity resulting from induced electron orbital motion under an external magnetic field. Unlike paramagnetic materials, this induced moment exhibits negligible temperature dependence as thermal agitation does not significantly affect the relevant electron orbits.

Consequently, $\chi$ remains constant and negative across all temperatures $T$.

The behavior shown in graph (A)—constant negative $\chi$ versus $T$—correctly represents diamagnetism. In contrast, graph (B) shows constant positive susceptibility, while graph (C) displays complex temperature variation, and graph (D) follows the $\chi \propto 1/T$ relationship characteristic of paramagnetism.

The correct representation corresponds to choice $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two bar magnets $A$ and $B$ are geometrically similar but the magnetic moment of $A$ is twice that of $B$. $T_1$ is the time period of oscillation when their like poles are kept together. When unlike poles are kept together, the time period of oscillation is $\mathrm{T}_2$. The ratio $\mathrm{T}_1: \mathrm{T}_2$ will be
questions.solution:
Magnetic moments and inertia: Let $M_A$ and $M_B$ be the magnetic moments, with $M_A = 2M_B$. Given geometric similarity, moments of inertia are equal: $I_A = I_B = I$.

The period of oscillation in uniform field $B$ is $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{I_{\text{net}}}{M_{\text{net}} B}}$.

Combined moment of inertia is $I_{\text{net}} = 2I$.

Like poles: Net magnetic moment adds: $M_{\text{net1}} = M_A + M_B = 3M_B$. Period is $T_1 = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{2I}{3M_B B}}$.

Unlike poles: Net magnetic moment subtracts: $M_{\text{net2}} = M_A - M_B = M_B$. Period is $T_2 = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{2I}{M_B B}}$.

The ratio is $\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M_B B / 2I}{3M_B B / 2I}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{3}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, so $T_1 : T_2 = 1 : \sqrt{3}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

$\mathrm{B} = \mu_0 (\mathrm{H} + \mathrm{M})$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Nickel shows ferromagnetic property at room temperature. If the temperature is increased beyond Curie temperature, then it will show
questions.solution: Nickel exhibits ferromagnetism because of a quantum physical effect called exchange coupling in which the electron spins of one atom interact with those of neighbouring atoms. The result is alignment of the magnetic dipole moments of the atoms, inspite of the randomizing tendency of atomic collisions. This persistent alignment is what gives ferromagnetic materials their permanent magnetism. If the temperature of a ferromagnetic material is raised above a certain critical value, called the Curie temperature, the exchange coupling ceases to be effective. Most such materials then become simply paramagnetic; that is, the dipoles still tend to align with an external field but much more weakly, and thermal agitation can now more easily disrupt the alignment.

questions.solution:
Let $\lambda$ be wavelength of monochromatic light, $d$ the distance between coherent sources, and $D$ the distance between screen and source, then fringe width is
$\quad \beta=\frac{D \lambda}{d}$ Given, $d_{1}=d, D_{1}=D, d_{2}=10 d, D_{2}=\frac{D}{2}\therefore \quad \quad \beta_{2}=\frac{\frac{D}{2} \lambda}{10 d}=\frac{D \lambda}{20 d}\Rightarrow \quad \beta_{2}=\frac{W}{20}$
